content: Hi all, does anyone know best practices for shipping a library that includes a ProofWidgets 4 widget? My guess is that we should just pre-build the JavaScript and ship that directly (since we can't guarantee that users will have the right build dependencies), but I'd be open to other workflows if that's a bad idea. If there's a project that does this particularly well that I could copy, I'd really appreciate a pointer.

Hi @Harry Goldstein! In ProofWidgets we do what you wrote - just ship the JS in the git repo. We relied on cloud releases in the past, but that has proven to be unreliable. We have a custom Lake target that updates package-lock.json, node_modules, and builds the JS from the TS. If you would find it useful, and are happy with using a comparable file layout (widget/ in your repo root), we could turn that target into a package facet so that you can use it to also build your JS.

We have a setup for that workflow that works, so no need to make the facet for our sake, but that might be helpful for other folks! Do you just gitignore all build artifacts other than the final built JS?
Yes gitignore node_modules and dist/ (typechecked but not bundled JS), check in the bundled JS.
